strongest_angle: Examine how Copenhagen Business School researchers Mary Uhl-Bien and Anders Trillingsgaard show that leadership emerges through ongoing interactions rather than just formal hierarchical positions.

key_facts.fact: Copenhagen Business School published an article on October 6, 2026, featuring Mary Uhl-Bien and Anders Trillingsgaard discussing how collective leadership emerges continuously through interactions between people.

Research published via the University of Warwick explores the intersection of collective and hierarchical leadership in a software engineering company in Turkey by analyzing 5 hours of video-recorded virtual team meetings.
The Association for Business Psychology published an article on October 13, 2026, examining who leads when the formal leader is not physically in the room.
London School of Economics published an article on March 12, 2026, detailing how successful teams navigate between flat and hierarchical structures.

numbers.label: Hours of video-recorded virtual team meetings analyzed
